This aligns with the current state of the field, where researchers work with modified versions of natural amino acids or entirely synthetic amino acid analogs, but not with complete mirror-image proteins.

The key distinction is that Statement 2 accurately reflects the limitation that mirror proteins remain beyond our current synthetic capabilities, while Statement 1 incorrectly suggests we can already incorporate mirror-image amino acid sequences into functional xenoproteins.
